name: When do I need a finish carpenter instead of a general rough carpenter for my bathroom?

mainEntity.name: When do I need a finish carpenter instead of a general rough carpenter for my bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: You need a finish carpenter when you want seamless transitions between walls, floors, and cabinetry, or when upgrading to custom features like beadboard, crown molding, and built-in nooks. Unlike rough framing, finish carpentry focuses on visible precision, tight joints, and seamless scribing against out-of-plumb walls. If you are replacing a vanity with a non-standard size or adding architectural character that drywall alone cannot provide, professional trim work is essential.
acceptedAnswer.description: You need a finish carpenter for visible, detail-oriented work such as custom trim, tight miter joints, vanity framing, and scribing molding against uneven walls.
